stories.title: New paper proposes cmHC to balance stream mixing in hyper-connections
stories.summary: Researchers introduce cmHC, a geometric-contraction method for mixing residual streams in hyper-connections without causing them to degenerate, aimed at improving training stability for multi-stream transformer architectures.
stories.more: Hyper-connections extend standard residual connections to multiple streams, and recent work constrains the resulting stream-mixing matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices, to stabilize residual propagation. This paper studies how to mix residual streams effectively within that polytope and identifies a mixing trade-off: residual matrices that stay too close to the polytope's vertices cause hyper-connections to degenerate. The excerpt cuts off before describing the proposed cmHC method's mechanism or reporting results.

stories.title: Paper benchmarks world models' failure to avoid object penetration
stories.summary: A new benchmark, NoPeBench, finds that no open-source video world model reliably prevents generated objects from penetrating obstacles, even though their hidden states already encode the information needed to predict it.
stories.more: The paper studies a previously unaddressed problem in interactive video world models: preventing generated objects from passing through physical obstacles. It introduces NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond when objects encounter obstacles. Testing finds that none of the open-source models evaluated can reliably avoid this failure. Surprisingly, the hidden states of diffusion transformers already contain the information needed to predict when a penetration violation would occur, suggesting the capability exists but isn't being used at generation time.

stories.title: Paper argues text-aware image super-resolution needs reasoning, not just vision
stories.summary: A new paper argues that restoring readable text in super-resolved images requires reasoning over context, not just visual restoration, since severely degraded text can't be read from local evidence alone.
stories.more: Text-aware image super-resolution aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content, and existing methods treat it purely as a visual restoration problem. The authors argue severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone, and that humans instead read it by reasoning over image context, logical patterns, and prior knowledge. This raises the paper's central question of whether the task needs reasoning, which it investigates using two diagnostic tools described in the excerpt but not detailed before it cuts off.

stories.title: ReSpaceBench benchmark tests AI agents' memory of previously visited rooms
stories.summary: ReSpaceBench is a new benchmark of 3,244 questions across 590 scenes testing whether embodied AI agents can recognize previously visited places despite viewpoint changes and distinguish them from similar rooms.
stories.more: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents that repeatedly operate in the same environments, requiring them to recognize revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguish them from similar-looking rooms, and update memories as environments change. The paper notes that existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. To address this, it introduces ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes. The excerpt is cut off before describing how current models perform on the benchmark.

stories.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview debuts as a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model
stories.summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a new mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35B total and 3B activated parameters that supports thinking-mode generation, combining recurrent memory with bidirectional attention.
stories.more: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is introduced as a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, and it supports thinking-mode generation. The model adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion, combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, using learnable block-size calibration. The excerpt does not give benchmark results or release details beyond the architecture description.

stories.title: MemOnce proposes scalable memory architecture to cut LLM context costs
stories.summary: MemOnce is a new memory architecture for LLMs aimed at long-horizon and continual interactions, addressing the linear memory growth and quadratic compute cost of standard Transformer KV caches.
stories.more: Deploying LLMs for long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, which existing architectures struggle with. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, causing linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as context expands. Linear-time architectures instead compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. MemOnce is introduced to address this tradeoff, though the excerpt cuts off before explaining its specific mechanism.

stories.title: Duopra paper tackles turning full-duplex chat agents into task-capable agents
stories.summary: The Duopra paper addresses getting full-duplex conversational AI agents, which already handle natural turn-taking and interruptions, to also reliably invoke tools and revise arguments after user corrections.
stories.more: Full-duplex interaction models already support natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions, giving them strong conversational agency. The paper argues that completing tasks also requires task agency: timely tool invocation and revising arguments after a user's corrections. It describes a frontend-backend agent split, where the frontend decides whether and what to request while the backend determines how to execute it. Execution can be offloaded to the backend, but unsent requests from the frontend can't be executed, which the paper identifies as a limitation of this separation. The excerpt is cut off before detailing Duopra's specific solution.
